solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Derbyshire's gully runs into Yorkshire opening bowler

indicators.note: something that runs into another thing goes inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Darren Gough, fast bowler who opened the attack for Yorkshire and England
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: a batsman's runs flowing into the figures of Yorkshire's opening bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside GOUGH to give GROUGH. Gough was a Yorkshire and England opening bowler; Derbyshire is an English county containing much of the Peak District.
explanation.definitionFit: A grough is a natural channel or fissure in peat moorland, a dialect word from the Peak District hills of northern England.

clue.text: Two experts, both caught out supporting Greek mythological sisters

indicators.note: a batsman caught out leaves, so the cricket letter for caught goes from each word
in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath, so this part comes after

blocks.note: Gr is the abbreviation for Greek
an ace is an expert, so two of them
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught, taken once from each ace

explanation.surface: Two specialists, both caught, propping up a Greek myth about sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek' reads as the adjective in 'Greek mythological sisters', but it also supplies GR. Each ACE loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: The Graeae were three grey-haired sisters in Greek myth who shared a single eye and tooth.

clue.text: Intervals excessive overlooking a considerable tenor cast

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooking means sitting above, so the first part comes on top
something cast is thrown off, so that letter is discarded

blocks.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive
taken as written
vast means very considerable in size
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A musical critique: the intervals are overdone, and a big tenor has been cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a singer's casting but means thrown off; OTT is the British abbreviation for over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottava is Italian for an octave, the musical interval spanning eight notes.

clue.text: Wee statuette? Fig leaves!

indicators.note: the verb leaves means departs, so those letters go from the word

blocks.note: a figurine is a small statue
taken as written

explanation.surface: A little statue whose modesty is preserved by fig leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fig leaves' looks like the nouns covering a nude statue; 'leaves' is a verb. FIGURINE loses FIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Wee is the informal British word for urine, as in having a wee.

clue.text: Mike underneath Georgia having sex

indicators.note: in a down clue, underneath means placed below, so this part follows

blocks.note: GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia
mic and mike are both short for microphone

explanation.surface: Mike is on the bottom, Georgia on top: a bedroom scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a racy one; 'having sex' means possessing sexual characteristics.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamic is a biological term for reproduction involving sexual union of gametes, so sexual or sexed.

clue.text: Stories about Catholic churchgoers

indicators.note: one thing placed about another surrounds it on both sides

blocks.note: a oner can be a big lie, a whopper, so stories in the sense of fibs
C is the standard abbreviation for Catholic

explanation.surface: Tales told about the Catholic faithful who fill the pews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stories' reads as tales but means lies: ONERS around C gives ONCERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oncers are people who attend church only once on a Sunday, a jocular term for occasional worshippers.

clue.text: Pool player of the month has work with champion, nothing less

indicators.note: less nothing means minus the round zero letter, so that letter goes

blocks.note: Oct is the calendar abbreviation for October
an opus is a work, especially of music
a hero is a champion
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A snooker or pool player of the month who works with the champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool player' suggests the cue game, but the pool is a swimming pool. HERO loses its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopush is underwater hockey, played on the bottom of a swimming pool, so an octopusher plays it.

clue.text: American at the rear gets derisive cheer in state

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a case is a state of affairs or condition
a boo is a jeer

explanation.surface: An American at the back of a crowd raises a mocking cheer in some state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' suggests a US state but means a condition. CASE holds BOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Caboose is American for the last carriage of a freight train, and also slang for the backside.

clue.text: Standard disc is striking

blocks.note: a rule is a standard or norm
a ring is a disc-like round shape

explanation.surface: A standard record is a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' reads as impressive, but means hitting; rulering is an old school punishment of rapping with a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruler someone is to strike them with a ruler, so rulering is a beating given with one.

clue.text: Pole by himself supplying old-fashioned spread

blocks.note: S, south, is one of the poles
per se is Latin for by itself

explanation.surface: A Pole working on his own supplies an old-style spread for bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' reads as a Polish man but is the South pole, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sperse is an obsolete, Spenserian shortening of disperse, meaning to scatter or spread.

clue.text: One disrupting US President will get returned on time or early retirement

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the president's name is read from right to left
a thing that disrupts breaks in among the letters, sitting inside the name
in an across clue, placed on means added after, so the time letter follows

blocks.note: Jimmy Carter, the 39th US President
the Roman numeral for one
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone causing trouble for an American president will see him sent back on schedule, an early retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early' flags an obsolete word: this is an old Spenserian form of retreat. 'on' places the time letter after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Retraict is a Spenserian, now obsolete, spelling of retreat, and a retreat is a withdrawal or retirement.

clue.text: Very boring moderation for a Madagascan

indicators.note: something boring drills into another thing, ending up inside it

blocks.note: hoa or ho is an old word for a halt, moderation or restraint
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A Madagascan finds moderation in all things tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' reads as dull but means drilling in. HOA takes V.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hova are the Merina people of central Madagascar, and a Hova is one of them.

clue.text: Figure of speech over in a new schedule

indicators.note: a word that is in another one sits within its letters

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a timetable is a schedule
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A rhetorical device turning up inside a fresh timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: A and N lead into TIMETABLE, which takes O in near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimetabole is the rhetorical figure that repeats words in reverse order, as in 'eat to live, not live to eat'.

clue.text: African rhino turning up in say, stream before yours truly

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means read from bottom to top, the reverse order

blocks.note: taken as written
eg, for example, is what say means
a nala or nullah is an Indian watercourse or stream
the setter refers to himself

explanation.surface: A rhinoceros in Africa surfacing in a stream ahead of the writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhino' is British slang for money, not the animal. INEGNALAME read upwards gives EMALANGENI.
explanation.definitionFit: Emalangeni is the plural of lilangeni, the currency unit of Eswatini (Swaziland), so African money.

clue.text: Ordinary member in cut coming back earnestly

indicators.note: coming back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the whole string reads right to left

blocks.note: O is an abbreviation for ordinary
M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP
taken as written
to axe something is to cut it

explanation.surface: An ordinary member of some body, caught up in cuts, returns in all seriousness.
explanation.walkthrough: O, M, IN and AXE make OMINAXE, which reversed is EX ANIMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex animo is Latin for 'from the heart', so it means sincerely or in earnest.

clue.text: One who's made a proposal married again

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for married
to do something over is to do it again

explanation.surface: Someone who once popped the question has gone and got married a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a marriage proposal; the definition means a formal proposal at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The mover of a motion is the person who formally proposes it at a meeting for debate.

clue.text: Newspaper has to pass on fine material

indicators.note: one thing that has another next to it is joined to it

blocks.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical, especially of a party
to pass away is to die; 'pass on' is split here

explanation.surface: A newspaper must pass along some quality cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass on' reads as one phrase, but 'to pass' gives DIE and 'on' joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, thin, stiffened cotton muslin used for dresses and trimmings.

clue.text: Victor's against more than one rowing in Shetland springs

indicators.note: against here means set right beside, so one piece is placed next to the other

blocks.note: Victor is the radio alphabet word for V
an oar is a rower, so oars are several people rowing

explanation.surface: A winner up against a crew of rowers in a Shetland regatta.
explanation.walkthrough: An oar can mean the person pulling it, as in 'a good oar'. Shetland is the island group north of mainland Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Voar is the Orkney and Shetland dialect word for the season of spring, from Old Norse.

clue.text: Scratch before squeezing a head on spot

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept
squeezing something means holding it tightly inside, so the pair goes within

blocks.note: ere is a poetic word for before
taken as written
the first letter of spot

explanation.surface: Picking at a spot on one's head before squeezing it.
explanation.walkthrough: ERE holds A and S between its R and final E.
explanation.definitionFit: To scratch something out is to erase or delete it, as with a name scratched from a list.

clue.text: Figures going around on Russian adviser

indicators.note: something going around another encircles it, holding it inside

blocks.note: stats are statistics, figures
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Statistics circulating about a Russian adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' meaning concerning gives RE, the Latin-derived word used in business letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A starets is a Russian Orthodox spiritual elder who acts as counsellor and adviser, like Rasputin.

clue.text: Pulls punches, relieving pressure

indicators.note: relieving something of a thing takes it away, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: plug is slang for a punch, as in 'plug someone'
P is the abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A boxer holds back the punches to ease the pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulls punches' looks like one idiom; 'Pulls' is the definition alone. PLUGS loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: To lug is to haul or drag something heavy, so lugs means pulls.

clue.text: Dissolute period? The opposite, time for prayer

blocks.note: fast means dissolute, so this reads as a spell of wild living
surface padding: a comment saying the real sense is the reverse of the first
a day of fasting and devotion

explanation.walkthrough: 'The opposite' warns that the first reading is a joke: the real sense is the reverse of wild living.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast day is a religious day of abstaining from food, given to penitence and prayer.

clue.text: Cross-shaped connection one's seen in opening

indicators.note: what is seen in something sits inside it

blocks.note: a chasm is a gaping opening
the Roman numeral for one; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A cross-shaped link visible in a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'one's' stands for is, so the clue reads 'one is seen in opening'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiasm is an X-shaped crossing, as of the optic nerves or of chromosomes.

clue.text: Harsh notes one's omitted around Christmas poem opening

indicators.note: something omitted is left out, so those letters disappear
around means turned about, so what remains is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: saw-tones are harsh, rasping sounds like a saw's
the letters of one's taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Discordant notes left out of a Christmas carol.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'one's' are removed exactly as printed, apostrophe ignored, before the remainder turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Clarke Moore's poem 'A Visit from St Nicholas' famously begins "'Twas the night before Christmas".

clue.text: Taking extra time and time again bent over

blocks.note: in printing jargon lean work is slow, poorly paid typesetting that takes extra time
time appears again in the clue, now abbreviated to T

explanation.surface: Spending more and more time hunched over something.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAN is a printers' term: lean copy is hard, time-consuming work, as opposed to fat. 'and' joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant is a past tense of lean, and to lean is to bend or incline the body over.

clue.text: Like some parties in sea around Malta

blocks.note: first meaning: built around a theme, like fancy-dress parties
second meaning: the Mediterranean, split into the article and its short name

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is two words run together: THE MED is the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: A themed party has a single unifying idea, such as a decade or costume, for decorations and dress.

clue.text: Sage Henry also known as Mark

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
aka is the standard abbreviation of also known as
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A wise man called Henry who also goes by the name Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' and 'Mark' look like a man's names but stand for unit symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: A hakam is a wise man or learned scholar, from the Hebrew and Arabic word for a sage.

clue.text: Finally back garden plot gets cut

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, so only its last letter is used

blocks.note: the last letter of back
an erf is a South African garden plot

explanation.surface: At last the back garden gets cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back garden' looks like one phrase; 'back' only gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerf is the slit or cut made by a saw, or the width of that cut.

clue.text: Soprano Eleanor is sharp, concerning the wind

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano
Nell is a short form of Eleanor

explanation.surface: A soprano called Eleanor is pitch-sharp when it comes to wind instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical picture misleads; the wind is weather here.
explanation.definitionFit: Snell is Scots for keen or biting, used especially of cold, piercing wind.

clue.text: Headbands given by number close to Midwest state?

definitions.note: TENIA is singular; the clue should read headband

indicators.note: close to means right next to, so the two parts are joined side by side

blocks.note: ten is a number
IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa

explanation.surface: Headbands supplied by a number of people near a Midwest state.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives tenia as a single headband, so the plural 'Headbands' is a slip in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenia, or taenia, is a ribbon or fillet worn round the head in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Unarmed soldier miles to the rear

indicators.note: this phrase sends the abbreviation for the distance unit from the front of the word round to its end

blocks.note: a miner is a soldier who digs tunnels, a sapper

explanation.surface: An unarmed soldier trudging miles behind the rest of his unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unarmed soldier' reads as one phrase, but 'Unarmed' is the definition. MINER's M goes to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Inerm is a botanical word for having no thorns or prickles, hence defenceless or unarmed.

clue.text: Suit includes unusually neat fur

indicators.note: a word that includes another holds it inside its own letters

blocks.note: gee is a dialect verb meaning to suit or go well with
nett can mean neat or pure, a sense the dictionary marks as rare

explanation.surface: An outfit trimmed with a surprisingly tidy fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' looks like an anagram signal but flags the rare sense of nett, meaning neat. GEE holds NETT.
explanation.definitionFit: Genette is the fur of the genet, a small spotted cat-like mammal related to the civets.

clue.text: One hint of departure poll to be considered further

indicators.note: a hint of something is just a trace, so only its first letter is used

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article, meaning one
the first letter of departure
a referendum is a public poll on a single question

explanation.surface: One sign that a country might leave is a vote on whether to go.
explanation.walkthrough: Published in 2019, the surface evokes the Brexit referendum on departing the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad referendum is a Latin diplomatic phrase for an agreement subject to further consideration by a higher authority.

clue.text: Worker behind tackles one having a long snout

indicators.note: a tackler wraps itself around its target, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: the worker ant is a crossword staple
behind schedule means late
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A labourer stands behind and grapples with a long-nosed creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackles' reads as a footballer's verb but means grips around; 'behind' means late, not rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Antliate is a zoological term for insects with a sucking proboscis, a spiral tongue or snout-like mouthpart.

clue.text: See this writer with poet take away business card

indicators.note: taking a letter away removes it from the word it belongs to

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself
a rishi is a Hindu sage or inspired poet
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: An instruction to meet the setter and a poet for a takeaway with business cards.
explanation.walkthrough: R as 'take' comes from the Latin recipe at the head of prescriptions. ME is followed by RISHI without its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Meishi is the Japanese word for the business card exchanged ceremonially at meetings.

clue.text: Excellent backing put across song subjected to criticism

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the word for excellent runs right to left
a word put across another stretches over it, so it sits outside

blocks.note: def is hip-hop slang for excellent
a lay is a ballad or song

explanation.surface: A great song is backed by critics who have panned it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excellent' becomes the hip-hop slang def, and 'backing' reads as musical accompaniment but means reversing.
explanation.definitionFit: To flay someone is to criticise them savagely, a figurative use of stripping off the skin.
